mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Even if Earth's axis turned to keep the north end facing the Sun all year, the Northern Hemisphere would still alternate between summer and winter.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: In June, the Northern Hemisphere has winter.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: In June, both hemispheres have summer.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: The Northern Hemisphere has summer in June because its tilt brings it closer to the Sun.

intelligence.enrichment: Earth's tilted axis, the maintenance of that tilt during revolution, and Earth's spherical shape make each hemisphere receive different sunlight intensity and different lengths of daytime at different times of year. A hemisphere tilted toward the Sun receives sunlight spread over a smaller area and more than 12 hours of daylight, producing summer; the opposite hemisphere receives weaker and shorter sunlight, producing winter. The learner correctly applies this rule: Earth's tilted axis, the maintenance of that tilt during revolution, and Earth's spherical shape make each hemisphere receive different sunlight intensity and different lengths of daytime at different times of year. Summer happens because Earth or the summer hemisphere is closer to the Sun.
